nodes.title: Eigenvalues and spectral norm of Hermitian matrices

nodes.summary: The eigenvalues of a positive semidefinite real matrix with nonnegative entries and row sums at most `1` lie in `[0, 1]`. Nonnegativity with the row-sum bound gives the upper bound `1`, symmetry makes the eigenvalues real, and positive semidefiniteness gives the lower bound `0`; positive semidefiniteness alone gives no upper bound.

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a complex square matrix whose rows and columns are indexed by a finite set $n$, and write $M^*$ for its conjugate transpose. If $M$ is normal, that is, $M^* M = M M^*$, then there exist a unitary matrix $P$ indexed by $n$ (so $P^* P = P P^* = I$) and a family of complex numbers $(d_i)_{i \in n}$ such that $P^* M P$ is the diagonal matrix with diagonal entries $d_i$.
nodes.title: Spectral theorem for normal matrices

nodes.summary: Let `K` be a positive semidefinite real matrix and `λ > 0`. A vector `z` satisfies the fixed-point equation `z = λ K (Y - z)` if and only if it solves the linear system `(I + λ K) z = λ K Y`, if and only if `z = (λ⁻¹ I + K)⁻¹ K Y`; and `(λ⁻¹ I + K)⁻¹ K = K (K + λ⁻¹ I)⁻¹`. nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a square matrix over a field $K$, with rows and columns indexed by a finite type, whose determinant is a unit of $K$ (so $M$ is invertible), and let $\mu \in K$ be nonzero. Then a vector $x$ is an eigenvector of $M$ with eigenvalue $\mu$ (that is, $x \ne 0$ and $Mx = \mu x$) if and only if $x$ is an eigenvector of $M^{-1}$ with eigenvalue $\mu^{-1}$.

Newton's identities for traces of matrix powers

nodes.summary: A real matrix with nonnegative entries whose row sums are all at most `1` has spectral radius at most `1`. The spectral radius is that of the complexified matrix, so it bounds the modulus of every complex eigenvalue, including nonreal eigenvalues of nonsymmetric matrices. The proof bounds it by the induced `∞` operator norm, the largest absolute row sum.
